name: Banking
one_liner: Banks take deposits and lend or invest them, earning the spread between asset yields and funding costs while managing credit, liquidity and capital constraints.
how_it_makes_money: The core engine is net interest income: interest earned on loans and securities minus interest paid on deposits and borrowings. Fee income adds card interchange, account and overdraft fees, wealth and asset management, and, at investment banks, advisory, underwriting and trading revenue.
revenue_formula: Revenue = net interest income + non-interest (fee) income
Net interest income = average earning assets × net interest margin
Fee income = customers × products per customer × fee per product
cost_structure: Interest expense: the cost of deposits and wholesale funding, highly sensitive to rate moves
Personnel: salaries and bonuses, the largest non-interest expense, especially in investment banking
Credit losses: loan-loss provisions that swing sharply with the economic cycle
Technology and operations: core systems, digital channels, cybersecurity
Branch network and occupancy: shrinking as customers shift to digital
Regulatory and compliance: AML/KYC, stress testing, reporting
margins: Well-run banks earn a return on equity of roughly 10-15% and efficiency ratios around 50-60%; the spread is driven by deposit franchise strength, credit discipline, scale, and fee mix.

key_metrics.name: Net interest margin (NIM)
key_metrics.what: Net interest income as a share of earning assets; the core profitability of the lending business.

key_metrics.name: Efficiency ratio
key_metrics.what: Non-interest expense divided by revenue; lower means a leaner bank.

key_metrics.name: Return on equity / tangible equity (ROE / ROTCE)
key_metrics.what: Profit relative to shareholder capital; the headline measure investors compare against the cost of equity.

key_metrics.name: CET1 ratio
key_metrics.what: Core equity capital over risk-weighted assets; the main regulatory measure of a bank's loss-absorbing cushion.

key_metrics.name: Net charge-off rate (NCO)
key_metrics.what: Loans written off net of recoveries as a share of loans; shows realized credit quality.

key_metrics.name: Loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR)
key_metrics.what: How much of the deposit base is lent out; signals liquidity and balance-sheet usage.

key_metrics.name: Deposit beta
key_metrics.what: How much of a policy-rate change the bank passes on to depositors; drives NIM through rate cycles.

trends: Deposit competition and funding costs remain a focus after the 2023 regional bank failures
Evolving capital rules (Basel III endgame) shape balance-sheet strategy for large banks
Consolidation among regional and community banks seeking scale
Digital-first challengers and embedded finance pressure retail economics
Generative AI adoption in operations, compliance and customer service
Private credit funds competing with banks for corporate lending

case_angles.question: A regional bank's profits have fallen despite loan growth. Why, and what should it do?
Should a mid-size bank acquire a neighboring regional bank?
How should a retail bank reduce its branch network cost while protecting deposits?
How should an incumbent bank respond to a digital-only bank winning young customers?

interview_hooks: Do branches still matter for gathering low-cost deposits, or is digital enough?
Is the shift of corporate lending to private credit a threat or a partnership opportunity for banks?
Should mid-size banks face the same capital and liquidity rules as the largest banks?
